vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: icp-filing
Version: 2.3.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate informational tool for ICP filing in China. The core logic in `scripts/icp.sh` consists of a Python script that provides checklists, workflow steps, and HTML snippets for website registration, with no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose (an ICP filing guide); it needs no credentials or installs and the included script only prints guidance — the main issue is a minor mismatch between the SKILL.md command names and the script's implemented commands.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included functionality: guidance about ICP filing, checklists, process and FAQ-style outputs. There is a minor inconsistency: SKILL.md documents commands like `guide`, `document`, `provider`, `timeline`, `faq` but the shipped script (`scripts/icp.sh`) implements `checklist`, `flow`, `query`, `province`, and `footer`. Nothing else requested (no env vars, no binaries) is disproportionate to an ICP guidance skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructions and the script stay within the stated scope: generating checklists, process steps, query instructions and footer HTML. The code does not read system configuration, request credentials, make network calls, or transmit data to external endpoints. SKILL.md does include an external feedback URL (bytesagain.com) but the skill does not programmatically call it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only). A local script file is included; it is plain Bash that runs an embedded Python snippet. No downloads, extract operations, or third-party package installs are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The code does not reference environment variables or secrets; requested access is proportionate to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system-wide configuration or modify other skills. It does not require elevated privileges or permanent presence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a local ICP filing guide with a small helper script. Before installing, consider: 1) Note the SKILL.md command list differs from the script's actual commands — confirm which commands your agent will call (the agent might attempt commands that don't exist). 2) Review the included script locally (scripts/icp.sh) to confirm outputs match your expectations — it only prints guidance and HTML footer snippets and does not contact networks or read secrets. 3) Because this is an instruction-only skill with an embedded script, run it in a safe environment to verify behavior if you have any doubt. If you plan to use it in automation, ensure the agent does not accidentally attempt to execute nonexistent commands listed in SKILL.md.
